findings.title: Delete menu item hidden when rulerRule is absent for Grafana-managed rules from list view
findings.body: `canDelete` is now computed from either rulerRuleAbility or grafanaPromRuleAbility, but the actual menu rendering condition at `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}` still requires `rulerRule` to be truthy. Since the whole point of this PR is to support the case where only `promRule` is available (ruler API removed from list view), delete action will never render for rules coming from the alert list view even when `canDelete` is true via `grafanaDeleteAbility`. `handleDelete` also requires a `RulerRuleDTO` parameter, so the API is inconsistent with the new partial-data flow.

findings.title: Pause menu item still gated on rulerRule only
findings.body: The pause menu item condition `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana'` requires rulerRule to be a grafana rule, but canPause can now become true purely from grafanaPauseAbility (based on promRule) without rulerRule being present. This means pause will never show in the alert-list-view context even though canPause is true, since MenuItemPauseRule requires a RulerRuleDTO rule prop that isn't present.

findings.title: Removed ruler rule matching no longer differentiates creating/deleting rule states
findings.body: The previous implementation fetched both ruler and Prometheus data and used matchRules to render 'Creating' (ruler-only) and 'Deleting' (prom-only) states via RuleOperation. This PR removes the ruler fetch and the matching logic entirely, rendering only Prometheus-sourced rules. As a result the UI will not show rules that exist only in ruler but haven't propagated to Prometheus yet (creating state), nor rules that still appear in Prometheus but were deleted from ruler (deleting state), effectively silently dropping these transitional states without a replacement implementation or test coverage for the removed behavior described by matchRules tests that were deleted.

findings.title: useRulerRuleAbility called with possibly undefined rule but still used for canEditRule logic unconditionally
findings.body: useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update) is called even when `rule` is undefined (RuleProps now allows either rule or promRule). While useAllRulerRuleAbilities tolerates undefined rule, mixing this with the new useGrafanaPromRuleAbility fallback obscures intent and risks returning stale/incorrect ability tuples (e.g., when both rule and promRule happen to be present but inconsistent, the OR logic could incorrectly grant edit permission based on whichever path returns true first).

findings.title: Comment above useAllAlertRuleAbilities refers to its own deprecated usage incorrectly
findings.body: The comment '// This hook is being called a lot...' was moved under useAllAlertRuleAbilities but it originally described performance concerns for that specific (now deprecated) hook. Since the hook now simply delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, the comment is misleading as placed - it implies the memoization optimization lives directly in this wrapper, but the actual heavy useMemo lives in useAllRulerRuleAbilities, called via delegation on every re-render of groupIdentifierV2 memo dependency on rule, which recomputes a new object identity whenever rule changes, potentially duplicating the concern rather than fixing it.
